utterances.text: Now, in this statement did he provide you with information as he saw fit, as he wanted to, or did you ask him any questions with respect to any of these individuals? Did you ask him whether he knew these individuals; and if so, did he see them, and so on and so on -- so forth? How did you take this statement? Can you remember?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: He voluntarily gave his statement at his own initiative, as he was born in the village of Petrovo in the Stimlje municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How far is Petrovo from Racak? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: About two kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You're saying the village of Petrovo is two kilometres away from the village of Racak; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's practically linked to Racak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, in his statement he mentioned the names of the KLA members from the village of Petrovo who were in the KLA in the village of Rance.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: If you want me to read out the names, then may we go into closed session for security reasons?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, may we comply with the witness's request for a closed or private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May I be heard on this? The suggestion as I understand it is that the identification of KLA members at the time is to be taken in private session for security reasons. I'm not sure at the moment whose security interests it is, whether it's the maker of the statement whose security concerns are involved or whether it's somebody else's. The Chamber will recall the experience we have had so far with researching statements of this kind and with our finding contrary material. Now, we've been able to do that thus far because we've been able to deal with the comparatively limited number of specific statements that have come our way through other witnesses and have been relied on by the accused. With 90 witness statements, that may well simply not be possible, and therefore there is from our point of view considerable advantage in this material being given publicly because this provides an additional opportunity for errors to be corrected by those who may see public broadcasts or read public reports of this material. So that although of course we're always respectful of legitimate security or other interests of individuals, I would invite the Chamber to be cautious before granting protective measures of the kind sought and to discover first the precise basis upon which they are being sought.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well, let me first ask the witness: Whose security is endangered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here specifically I mean the security of the individual who gave the statement as well as the security of his -- and safety of his family, because to the present day in Kosovo 13 and Metohija, as I've already said, there are former KLA members, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted) and terror is being exerted towards Albanians themselves, that is to say those Albanians who associated with ethnic Serbs and members of the police force, and so on and so forth. And I should also like to mention this: In the period -- or, rather, the Albanians told us that in the period from the 12th of June 1999, to the present day, a number of Albanians have been killed, and all knowledge about this indicates that they were killed by former KLA members. If need be, I can give you the names of the individuals who were killed, those that I can remember now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kay, on this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It occurs to me that we should have a redaction from the transcript because the particular individual in tab 1.1 was mentioned as to his place and occupation, and if that could be attended to straight away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. That will be redacted. The court deputy will bring me the relevant page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. It seems to me that it's the author of the statement who is really the person at risk here rather than the people whose names are disclosed within the documents, but that in dealing with this material one should be concerned to protect and make sure that no pointers are given as to name or identity of the maker of the statement and that that should be dealt with in an oblique way. We have the written materials before us, so it's very easily done. It can be referred to as the individual in tab 1 of the exhibit who made the statement. Any identifying factors can be dealt with obliquely and avoided, and the particular names can be just looked at in the document because we can see them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I just -- sorry, to add a sentence. This, of course, is exactly the problem that's concerning us. Just to assist the Trial Chamber in seeing it from our point of view, if you go, for example, to page -- to enclosure 1.51 -- sorry, 151, yes, you'll see its numbered at the top right-hand corner 03032848, you will see a statement with which you will be, I think, familiar because this is one of the statements -- it's about halfway through the file. 1.51. I'm waiting for His Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Tab 47.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes. You will see a statement with which you'll probably be familiar, because this is one of those that was referred to with an earlier witness. On that occasion, the witness was referred to -- not the witness, the maker of the statement was referred to without, I think, any protective measures at all, and on that occasion it was possible to approach the maker of the statement, and on that occasion the maker of the statement made a contrary statement. I know it hasn't been admitted as an exhibit. That is another issue. In those circumstances, the material, it was possible for us to lay material about that statement before the Court, and indeed this statement was the subject of cross-examination in the other case, the Limaj case, although I haven't immediately got my fingers on whether the name of the maker of the statement was given publicly in that case. It doesn't matter. Our concerns, as I explained before, but perhaps it's helpful to see it again with this statement before you, our concerns are that if -- yes. Our concerns are that if statement makers such as the statement maker here have accounts of the making of the statement that they would want to give, if the material is only given in closed session or in any other way where they cannot know what is attributed to them, and if we aren't able to or may decide not to investigate these matters by approaching 91 witness or 90-odd witness statement makers, then the possibility of correction is reduced by the closed session technique. That's my concern. Thank you for allowing me to make that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, anything on this point?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, first of all I wish like to apologise to the witness for not having asked at the very outset whether this name can be used. It was my understanding that it could be used. Later on, the witness said, and I assume that it was only his professional conscience that dictated him to do so, and knowing that in Kosovo it's not a good thing to mention the names of persons who gave statements because they may suffer consequences because terror reigns there, and he explained why. He's not in contact with these people, so he cannot say whether they are threatened now and to what extent. He only believes that, generally speaking, in relation to the situation in Kosovo it would not be desirable as far as the safety and security of these persons is concerned to have their names read out. So you can assess yourselves whether his request is justified or not. While preparing this witness, I did not have occasion to go into these matters. As soon as the witness mentioned this, I suggested to you to comply with what he requested. It seems so logical to me that if somebody can be endangered, that that should be prevented. And you know what the situation is like there: Anybody who ever gave a statement of this kind, is under threat. We can use all these documents without referring to the actual names of the persons who gave the statements when the witness says that we should not mention the names. I presume that this would not pertain to all of these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: A part of the difficulty, Mr. Milosevic, is something that you just said; the witness is not able to identify any particular security concern in relation to the witness, this particular witness, it's that he belongs to a group and anybody in that group, in that category, might be endangered. So there's nothing that specifically relates to the witness personally. It's the group to which he belongs. But I'll consider it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice or Mr. Kay or Mr. Milosevic, do you know how this matter was dealt with in the other case in which this witness testified, Limaj?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: My recollection is that there were some parts of the testimony that didn't immediately match the testimony that's going to be given here, I think, to do with informers, that were given in closed session. I believe that these particular statements, which weren't informer based statements, were dealt with in open session. I'll just confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Because of the volume of names, we're unable to identify that. It would take a bit of time to try and work that out from those transcripts. We looked at them under an entirely different way when we were researching them. Yes. Those names, those three names, were given in open session, of the witnesses whose transcripts were produced in the earlier cross-examination. The other names, of course, from the file that we have, that was not evidential material in that case. This file here arrives with the witness for the Defence in this trial. It was being used in a different way in the Limaj case, as a Prosecution witness with different materials. These documents essentially in this binder come through him. He brought them here in the same way that the witness Marinkovic brought her file including the statements as examples of investigations she had been concerned with at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm slightly surprised at that because he didn't come here expecting to give evidence in this case. He presumably brought documents because he was coming to give evidence in the Limaj case, and surely more of these -- some of these, at least, were used in that case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I might be wrong about that, but that was my assumption working on it. It may require some investigation or explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: If we were to have the evidence given in public session without any reference to the name of the author of the statement, that might be sufficient protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That would be very prudent and sufficient. This witness has got no interest, so to speak, with the Albanian community, as the Court would have seen. He's been responsible, in our submission, in relation to the information that he has gathered during his duties as a police officer. He's plainly working in a different area now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I took this statement, I had the same kind of job. This was on the 22nd of August, 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm afraid that there is a bit of a misunderstanding in terms of what Mr. Kay said a few moments ago, that he took statements when he worked as a policeman and that he now has a different job. Broadly speaking, he is certainly a policeman, and he certainly does the same kind of work as he did then. That's the kind of work he does now. He is a police inspector involved in crime investigation. He was a police inspector at that time in the crime investigation department, as he is now. So he has exactly the same job now as he had then when he took the statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll continue with the evidence in public session, but there should be no reference to the name of the author. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand that. Yes. I will call the person, say, Person A.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The person from tab 1.1, deal with it that way. Mr. Jasovic, did you have in mind the danger that the person who gave the statement to you may be subjected to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, because this kind of thing happens in Kosovo until the present day. As I said earlier on, many Albanians were killed from 1999 onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. In this statement that you got, on the bottom of the original page of your note or, rather, the statement that you and your colleague Sparavalo took, it says that "The following persons are within the ranks of the KLA," and then there is a long list of names. Are all of these persons from Racak and the surrounding area, Rance, Racak, Petrovo? Tell us, please, Racak, Rance, Petrovo, is all of that a relatively small area with about one or two or three kilometres in diameter?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I've already said two kilometres between Racak and Rance, three kilometres, and that's the same distance as between Rance and Petrovo. Person A gave the names of the members of the KLA from Petrovo because that is the place of residence of the said persons as well as the names of the KLA members from Racak who were in the village of Rance and the KLA there, where KLA headquarters were established in the beginning of June 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. When you turn the page, the list continues, doesn't it? And you have ten or 15 members of the KLA here who are described in this statement.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: At the outset it says that it is the 22nd of August, 1998, that the interview was conducted with this person, and then his details are set out. And here at the very end there is something else that was written, and there's a signature, and there's a handwritten date, the 26th of August, 1998. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. The date and the signature concerned are the date when the statement was sent on further to the relevant department in Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We want you to explain that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was the regular way it was done, with a signature and the relevant date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, Mr. Jasovic, to the best of your knowledge that you had at the time, what was the immediate reason for taking this action in Racak?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, the immediate reason was the terrorist attack and killing of policeman Svetislav Przic, who was killed from one of the numerous ambushes that were there. I can say that the action was preceded by the following: Before Svetislav Przic's killing, from the month of June until January when the said person was killed, a great many terrorist acts had been carried out against civilians of both Serb and Albanian ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's just look at a very specific piece of information. Please look at tab 1.49. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Should the name of the person who gave the statement be mentioned or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I'd rather not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. This person mentioned here gave a statement to you. Could you please comment upon this statement. Is there any information here that relates to the killing of the policeman?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: I can confirm the authenticity of this statement. The statement was signed by the interviewed person as well as by myself and by my colleague Momcilo Sparavalo. This is also a person who came of his own free will to the Secretariat of the Interior in Urosevac. As far as I can see from the statement, he gave the names of the members of the KLA from the village of Malopoljce, municipality of Stimlje, and the potential perpetrators of the terrorist attack against the policeman Svetislav Przic. In the statement he mentioned that the following persons, who were members of the KLA came from the village of Malopoljce, municipality of Stimlje, and they are the ones who killed Svetislav Przic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. At the end of the first paragraph of this statement of yours, he says how they were dressed and armed, and towards the end, in the last third of this big paragraph, it says that there was an armed attack at the patrol of the MUP of Serbia, and then at the very end he says: "He also told us that after the armed attack and killing, the three of them walked back to the village of Jezerce while he," the person in question, "went to the village of Malopoljce." So there is a description there as to what happened as far as the killing of the policeman was concerned. Is that what this statement contains?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It contains the first and last names of the persons concerned and also what his relative told him, that from an ambush near the Urosevac-Stimlje road in the village of Slivovo they opened fire from firearms at the police patrol that was moving from Stimlje towards Urosevac, and he mentions that an automatic weapon was fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. How was this statement taken? Everybody can read this statement, but how was it taken?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: The statement was taken on the basis of the Law on Criminal Procedure and its provisions in the prescribed manner, and as I have said, I confirm the authenticity of this statement because the person signed it, the interviewee signed it, and the interviewer, that is myself and my colleague Mr. Sparavalo, signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, did this person come in of their own accord to make the statement or were they apprehended? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC
utterances.text: No. The person came of his own accord. I knew the person from before, so that's why they came and volunteered.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now, would you look at tab 1.54, please, and the statement given to you by another person, and there are some things here that are linked to the event in Racak. And just a few tabs on you'll find tab 1.54. I hope you've found the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I'm sorry that I have to stop, but at first I thought there was no hearing, but I've been informed that there will be a hearing this afternoon, which means that we have to stop immediately. So just bear in mind the question you asked, and we'll come back to that tomorrow morning. We're adjourned until tomorrow morning at 9.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 26th day of April, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
